title: Runtime: select hardware tuning profile by GPU SKU + driver/CUDA (with override precedence + startup logging)
author: Yuki Sato
release_notes: Runtime now deterministically selects a tuning profile based on detected GPU SKU and driver/CUDA version. Adds explicit override precedence (fleet default < control-plane < per-customer pin < local/env) and emits a structured startup log line summarizing detection + selected profile. No behavior change if profile pack is disabled.
description:
Context
This is the first cut of deterministic profile selection for the Hardware tuning profiles pack project. We already have profile definitions + schema validation behind a flag (PR #24873). This PR wires selection into runtime startup + model load so we can (a) make selection predictable, (b) enforce compatibility gates, and (c) make on-call triage easier via explicit logging.

What this PR changes
- Adds a runtime selector that chooses a profile_id from the profile pack based on:
  - gpu.sku (H100 / L40S today; B200 intentionally treated as unsupported here and handled in follow-up gate work)
  - gpu.form_factor when present (SXM vs PCIe) to allow divergent defaults in future
  - driver version + cuda runtime version (used to enforce a minimum supported matrix per profile)
  - runtime features present (e.g., “supports_flash_attention_v3”) as optional qualifiers (non-blocking for now; logged)
- Defines override precedence (highest wins), with explicit audit-friendly reasons emitted in logs:
  1) CLI flag: --runtime.profile_id / --runtime.profile_version (local debugging / Private)
  2) Env vars: REDWOOD_PROFILE_ID / REDWOOD_PROFILE_VERSION (lab / canary)
  3) Control-plane config: fleet default profile (Hosted/Dedicated)
  4) Pack default selection rule (deterministic mapping)
- Adds structured startup log entry and periodic “active profile” log on model load:
  - Fields: profile_id, profile_version, selection_reason, detected_sku, driver_version, cuda_version, pack_checksum
  - Also logs a warning when an override is present (to avoid “mystery perf” during incident response)
- Adds a small compatibility helper:
  - If detected driver/cuda is outside the supported range for the selected profile: runtime refuses to start when a user explicitly pinned the profile_id (fail-fast), otherwise falls back to the next-most-compatible profile and logs the fallback reason.

Why
- We have fleet heterogeneity (driver/CUDA spread; PCIe vs SXM) and need profile selection to be deterministic and explainable.
- SRE asked that rollouts be observable and reversible; selection_reason + pack checksum are the minimum on-call debug surface.

Implementation notes
- Selection occurs at runtime startup after hardware probe and before model server initializes.
- Model-load path reuses the same selected profile snapshot to prevent “profile drift” if hardware metadata changes mid-process; selection is not re-run on every request.
- The selector is deterministic given the same inputs (unit tests cover ordering + tie-break rules).

Follow-ups (intentionally not in this PR)
- B200 hard compatibility gate + require explicit profile_version pin (tracked in ENG-4928; implemented in PR #24927).
- Exporting profile_id as a metric label (tracked in ENG-4931; implemented separately to manage cardinality).

Testing
- Unit tests for override precedence and selection tie-breaks.
- Golden tests for common fleet combos:
  - H100-SXM / driver 550.xx / CUDA 12.4
  - H100-PCIe / driver 545.xx / CUDA 12.3
  - L40S / driver 545.xx / CUDA 12.3
- Manual: validated on benchmark-lab H100 node; startup log includes expected selection_reason.

Checklist
- [x] Deterministic selection rules documented inline (selector.go)
- [x] Override precedence implemented and tested
- [x] Logs include reason + hardware/driver context
- [x] No behavior change when profile pack feature flag is disabled

Review conversation (highlights)
Noah Patel: The fallback behavior worries me. If we silently select a different profile due to compat, perf changes could be subtle. Can we make this explicit and gate it somehow?
Yuki Sato: Agreed. Updated: if the operator/customer explicitly pinned profile_id/profile_version and compat fails -> hard error. Only auto-fallback when selection is implicit (no pin) and we can pick a compatible default. Also added a WARN log with selection_reason=compat_fallback.

Irene Choi: Please confirm how we’re parsing driver versions. We’ve seen “550.54.15” vs “550.54” in fleet metadata; also make sure we log raw values.
Yuki Sato: Updated parser to accept 2-4 segments and compare semver-ish lexicographically by int segments. Added logging of raw_driver_string and normalized_driver_version.

Quentin Harris: Where does the compat matrix live? I want it versioned with the profile pack, not embedded in runtime.
Yuki Sato: Matrix is read from the pack metadata (min_driver, max_driver, min_cuda) per profile. Runtime only implements the evaluation function + tie-break ordering. Added tests to ensure schema validation rejects profiles missing compat ranges.

Benji Okafor: Override precedence needs guardrails in Dedicated. Even if we support env var/flag for Private, Hosted should not allow random env overrides.
Yuki Sato: Good call. Implemented deployment_mode gating: in Hosted/Dedicated, env var overrides are ignored unless allow_unsafe_overrides=true (only set in benchmark-lab). Still logs that an override was requested but ignored.

Sean Gallagher: Please add one single-line startup log that on-call can grep. Current log is split across multiple lines.
Yuki Sato: Updated to emit a single JSON log line at INFO with all fields; additional detail remains at DEBUG.

CI / checks
- build-and-unit-tests: PASS
- runtime-integration-smoke: PASS
- lint: PASS
- config-schema-golden-tests: PASS

Notes for release
- This PR is safe to merge behind the existing profile pack feature flag; selection is invoked only when the pack is enabled.
- When enabled, selection is deterministic and logs the chosen profile + reason; no metrics changes here.
commits: runtime/profile: add ProfileSelector interface and deterministic selection rules
runtime/profile: implement override precedence (flag/env/control-plane/default) with selection_reason logging
runtime/profile: add driver/CUDA compatibility evaluation + fallback behavior
tests: add golden matrices for H100/L40S driver/CUDA combinations
ops: emit structured startup log line for active profile
